citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).
record_used: subject S002, baseline run R02 (eyes-closed rest), occipital channels O1 and Oz, first 10 s (1600 samples) at 160 Hz -- the SAME git-tracked pair the sibling PLV and PLI cases use.
pipeline: readRDS(o1_s002r02) + readRDS(oz_s002r02) -> PhysioCrossModal::weightedPLI(freq_band=c(8,13), debiased=TRUE): band-pass both channels to alpha, form the analytic signals (Hilbert), take the imaginary cross-spectrum Im(analytic_O1 * conj(analytic_Oz)) per time point, and compute wPLI = |sum(Im)|/sum(|Im|) and the debiased wPLI (Vinck 2011 Eq. 6). The reference re-computes wPLI with an independent scipy pipeline (butter+filtfilt+hilbert) and demonstrates the debiasing on constructed independent / lagged / zero-lag signals (via reticulate). Deterministic (the demo is seeded).
note: The tracked inputs are eval/data/plv-eeg/{o1,oz}_s002r02.rds. The weighted phase-lag index (Vinck 2011) is the recommended modern EEG phase-connectivity measure: it is volume-conduction-robust (built from the IMAGINARY cross-spectrum, ~0 for zero-lag coupling) AND debiased (removes the sample-size positive bias of PLI/coherence). weightedPLI is validated by (a) reproducing an independent scipy imaginary-cross-spectrum wPLI to ~7e-3 (agreement, filtfilt-limited); and (b) demonstrating the debiasing -- for INDEPENDENT (uncoupled) signals the biased wPLI is spuriously positive (0.038) but the debiased wPLI is ~0 (0.0006, corrected), while genuine lagged coupling keeps a debiased wPLI of 1.0 and zero-lag stays ~0. The finding: the real O1-Oz debiased wPLI is low (0.011, like the PLI 0.016) -- the strong occipital alpha PLV (0.92) is dominated by volume conduction, now confirmed with the debiased state-of-the-art measure. The debiased wPLI can go slightly negative for uncoupled signals, which is expected of an unbiased estimator.
